text:
This component efficiently displays arbitrarily positioned cells using windowing techniques.
Cell position is determined by an injected cellPositioner property.
Windowing is vertical; this component does not support horizontal scrolling.
 Rendering occurs in two phases:

First pass uses estimated cell sizes (provided by the cache) to determine how many cells to measure in a batch.
Batch size is chosen using a fast, naive layout algorithm that stacks images in order until the viewport has been filled.
After measurement is complete (once the render has been committed) this component evaluates positioned cells
in order to determine if another measurement pass is required (eg if actual cell sizes were less than estimated sizes).
All measurements are permanently cached (keyed by keyMapper) for performance purposes.
Second pass uses the external cellPositioner to layout cells.
At this time the positioner has access to cached size measurements for all cells.
The positions it returns are cached by Masonry for fast access later.
Phase one is repeated if the user scrolls beyond the current layout's bounds.
If the layout is invalidated due to eg a resize, cached positions can be cleared using recomputeCellPositions().

 Animation constraints:
Simple animations are supported (eg translate/slide into place on initial reveal).
More complex animations are not (eg flying from one position to another on resize).
 Layout constraints:
This component supports multi-column layout.
The height of each item may vary.
The width of each item must not exceed the width of the column it is "in".
The left position of all items within a column must align.
(Items may not span multiple columns.)
title: Masonry component props

headings.title: children
headings.text:
Function responsible for rendering 2 or more virtualized components.
It is passed the current scroll and size values (clientHeight, clientWidth, scrollHeight, scrollLeft, scrollTop, scrollWidth),
an onScroll callback that should be passed through to the virtualized children that the user can scroll,
and a registerChild function that returns a ref callback for each virtualized child that should be kept in sync
(e.g. <Grid ref={registerChild("body")} onScroll={onScroll} />).
The scroll and size values can also be used for custom rendering (e.g. shading based on the scroll offset).

text: ScrollSync simplifies the process of synchronizing scrolling between two or more virtualized components. The example below uses three Grids to mimic a spreadsheet with a fixed header row and a fixed first column. Scroll the body of the spreadsheet; the header and first column follow along. It also shows how the scroll values can be used to control other UI, such as background colors. ScrollSync uses a render function as its children. Use the registerChild parameter to register each virtualized component that should be kept in sync (e.g. <Grid ref={registerChild("header")} />), and pass the onScroll parameter to the component(s) the user scrolls. Whenever a scroll offset is reported through onScroll, ScrollSync scrolls the other registered components to match it (only the axes that changed are synced) and calls the render function again with the updated values. The render function receives: registerChild(key): returns a ref callback that registers a component (such as a Grid) under a unique key onScroll: pass this to the scrollable component(s) scrollLeft, scrollTop: the current scroll offsets (e.g. for custom rendering) clientHeight, clientWidth: the size of the visible portion of the scrolled component scrollHeight, scrollWidth: the total size of all rows and columns in the scrolled component Version 10 removed the scrollLeft and scrollTop props from Grid; register the components with registerChild instead of passing the scroll offsets to them. For the common case of fixed header rows and/or columns, also take a look at MultiGrid, which handles this layout for you.
title: ScrollSync

text: GitHub is the easiest place to look for help, but it's probably not the fastest. This project is maintained by a single developer so there is limited bandwidth for answering questions. I recommend asking questions on Stack Overflow or Reddit to start with. Both sites have active communities who often respond quickly. If you don't find an answer there you can try opening a GitHub issue- but please take a moment first to see if your question has has already been answered before opening a new one.
title: Support

headings.title: Column sizes
headings.text: Column sizes A column's width is its flex basis. Columns can grow (flexGrow, defaults to 0) to fill unused space, or shrink (flexShrink, defaults to 1) when there is not enough room, within the bounds of minWidth and maxWidth. See the Column props for more.

headings.title: Column components
headings.text: Column components Column doesn't render anything itself: Table reads the props of its children (applying the Column defaults, also exported as defaultColumnProps) to render headers and cells. Falsy children are ignored, so columns can be shown or hidden conditionally. Because the defaults are applied to any child element, a component that wraps Column can be used as a column as well, e.g. const NameColumn = (props: ColumnProps) => <Column {...props} /> rendered as <NameColumn dataKey="name" label="Name" width={120} />. (The wrapper itself is never rendered, so it should only forward or compute props.) In version 10, Column is a function component; subclassing Column (class MyColumn extends Column) is no longer supported. Use a wrapper component instead. Next, learn how to style rows and use dynamic row heights, customize cells and headers or entire rows, or sort a table.

text: Table renders tabular data with a fixed header and windowed rows, for improved performance with large data sets. Its layout is created with flexboxes, and it uses a Grid internally to render only the rows that are visible. A table requires an explicit width and height, the height of its header (headerHeight) and rows (rowHeight), the number of rows (rowCount), and a rowGetter function that returns the data for a given row index. Its children are one or more Columns, each describing a column's header and the row attribute (dataKey) its cells display. The default table styles are in react-virtualized/styles.css; they only need to be imported once. The customizing styles guide explains how to override them. The example above uses AutoSizer to fill the available width. Table content can scroll vertically, but it is not meant to scroll horizontally. Columns shrink and grow to fit the table's width; consider using a MultiGrid for data with many columns.
title: Rendering a table

text: Each Column accepts three functions that control what its cells and header render: cellDataGetter returns a cell's data, given its dataKey, rowData, and columnData. The default (defaultTableCellDataGetter) reads rowData[dataKey] (or calls rowData.get(dataKey) for Map-like objects). Override it if your data is calculated or requires custom processing. cellRenderer renders a cell's contents, given its cellData, columnData, columnIndex, dataKey, isScrolling, parent, rowData, and rowIndex. The default (defaultTableCellRenderer) displays the cell data as a string. Override it if your data is some other type of object or requires custom formatting. headerRenderer renders the column header, given its columnData, dataKey, disableSort, label, sortBy, and sortDirection. The default (defaultTableHeaderRenderer) displays the label along with a sort indicator if the table is sorted by this column. The columnData prop can be used to pass additional data (e.g. action creators or relational data) to all three of these functions.
title: Custom cells and headers

headings.title: dataKey
headings.text:
Uniquely identifies the row-data attribute corresponding to this cell
(eg this might be "name" in an array of user objects).

headings.title: width
headings.text:
Flex basis (width) for this column;
This value can grow or shrink based on flexGrow and flexShrink properties.

headings.title: aria-label
headings.text: Optional aria-label value to set on the column header.

headings.title: cellDataGetter
headings.text:
Callback responsible for returning a cell's data, given its dataKey:
({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, rowData: any }): any.
 The default cellDataGetter expects to operate on either a vanilla Object or a Map-like object with a get method.
You should override it if your data is calculated or requires any custom processing.
Defaults to defaultTableCellDataGetter.

headings.title: cellRenderer
headings.text:
Callback responsible for rendering a cell's contents:
({ cellData: any, columnData: any, columnIndex: number, dataKey: string, isScrolling: boolean, parent: TableImperativeAPI, rowData: any, rowIndex: number }): ReactNode.
 The default cellRenderer (defaultTableCellRenderer) displays an attribute as a simple string.
You should override it if your data is some other type of object or requires custom formatting.

headings.title: className
headings.text: Optional CSS class to apply to the rendered cell container.

headings.title: columnData
headings.text:
Additional data passed to this column's cellDataGetter, cellRenderer, and headerRenderer.
Use this object to relay action-creators or relational data.

headings.title: defaultSortDirection
headings.text: Default sort order when clicked for the first time.

headings.title: disableSort
headings.text: If sort is enabled for the table at large, disable it for this column.

headings.title: flexGrow
headings.text: Flex grow style.

headings.title: flexShrink
headings.text: Flex shrink style.

headings.title: headerClassName
headings.text: Optional CSS class to apply to this column's header.

headings.title: headerRenderer
headings.text:
Optional callback responsible for rendering a column's header contents:
({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, disableSort: boolean, label: ReactNode, sortBy: string, sortDirection: SortDirection }): ReactNode.
 The default headerRenderer (defaultTableHeaderRenderer) displays the column label along with a sort indicator if the column is sort-enabled and active.

headings.title: headerStyle
headings.text: Optional inline style to apply to this column's header.

headings.title: id
headings.text: Optional id to set on the column header; used for the cells' aria-describedby.

headings.title: label
headings.text: Header label for this column.

headings.title: maxWidth
headings.text: Maximum width of column; this property will only be used if flexGrow is greater than 0.

headings.title: minWidth
headings.text: Minimum width of column.

headings.title: style
headings.text:
Optional inline style to apply to the rendered cell container.
 Table reads these props from each of its children (with the defaults above, exported as defaultColumnProps, applied), so components that wrap Column work as columns too; subclassing Column is no longer supported. See column components.

title: Column component props

headings.title: forceUpdateGrid
headings.text:
forceUpdateGrid Forcefully re-render the inner Grid component.
Calling forceUpdate on Table may not re-render the inner Grid since it uses shallowCompare as a performance optimization.
Use this method if you want to manually trigger a re-render.
This may be appropriate if the underlying row data has changed but the row sizes themselves have not.

headings.title: getOffsetForRow
headings.text:
getOffsetForRow Gets offset for a given row and alignment (align; alignment is a deprecated alias).
The alignment defaults to "auto"; an index of -1 (the default) refers to the last row.

headings.title: getScrollbarWidth
headings.text: getScrollbarWidth Gets the scrollbar width used to pad the table-header.

headings.title: invalidateCellSizeAfterRender
headings.text:
invalidateCellSizeAfterRender Invalidate the size of a row (after the current render has been committed); see Grid#invalidateCellSizeAfterRender.
This method is intended for CellMeasurer.

headings.title: measureAllRows
headings.text:
measureAllRows Pre-measure all rows in a Table.
Typically rows are only measured as needed and estimated heights are used for cells that have not yet been measured.
This method ensures that the next call to getTotalSize() returns an exact size (as opposed to just an estimated one).

headings.title: recomputeRowHeights
headings.text:
recomputeRowHeights Recompute row heights and offsets after the specified index (defaults to 0).
Table has no way of knowing when its underlying list data has changed since it only receives a rowHeight property.
If the rowHeight is a number it can compare before and after values but if it is a function that comparison is error prone.
In the event that a dynamic rowHeight function is in use and the row heights have changed this function should be manually called by the "smart" container parent.
This method will also force a render cycle (via forceUpdate) to ensure that the updated measurements are reflected in the rendered table.

headings.title: recomputeGridSize
headings.text:
recomputeGridSize Recompute row heights and offsets after the specified row index (defaults to 0); see Grid#recomputeGridSize.
(The column index is ignored.) This method is intended for CellMeasurer; also see recomputeRowHeights.

headings.title: scrollToCell
headings.text:
scrollToCell Ensure the specified row is visible (scrolling if necessary); the column index is ignored.
This allows a Table to be used with ArrowKeyStepper; also see scrollToRow.

headings.title: scrollToPosition
headings.text:
scrollToPosition Scroll to the specified vertical offset; scrollLeft is ignored (tables don't scroll horizontally).
Offsets are clamped to the scrollable range. This allows a Table to be used with ScrollSync.
Useful for animating position changes.
If the Table has a scrollElement, the scroll element (e.g. the window) is scrolled instead.

headings.title: scrollToRow
headings.text:
scrollToRow Ensure the row at the specified index is visible (scrolling if necessary).
This method can be used to safely scroll back to a row that a user has scrolled away from even if it was previously scrolled to.
The align parameter (default "auto") controls the alignment of the row:
"auto" scrolls the least amount possible to ensure that the specified row is fully visible
(a row taller than the table is aligned to its start, so that its start is visible);
"start" aligns the row to the top of the table and "end" to the bottom; "center" aligns it in the middle.
This is a one-time scroll: the row is not kept in view afterwards (e.g. if the table's size or its row heights change).
Rows that haven't been measured yet (e.g. by CellMeasurer) are positioned using their estimated heights.
If the Table has a scrollElement, the scroll element (e.g. the window) is scrolled instead.

headings.title: Calling methods
headings.text: Calling methods Table's methods can be called through a ref. The example below uses scrollToRow (with an align parameter) and scrollToPosition. As with List, these are one-time scrolls (the row isn't kept in view if the table's size or row heights change afterwards). In version 10, these methods replace the scrollToIndex, scrollToAlignment and scrollTop props.

text: Public (imperative) methods of a Table instance.
title: Table methods

headings.title: rowCount
headings.text: Number of rows in table.

headings.title: rowGetter
headings.text:
Callback responsible for returning a data row given an index:
({ index: number }): any.

headings.title: rowHeight
headings.text:
Either a fixed row height (number) or a function that returns the height of a row given its index:
({ index: number }): number.

headings.title: width
headings.text: Width of the table.

headings.title: aria-label
headings.text: ARIA label set on the outer Table element.

headings.title: aria-labelledby
headings.text: ARIA labelledby attribute set on the outer Table element.

headings.title: cellRangeRenderer
headings.text:
Responsible for rendering a group of cells given their index ranges.
 This is an advanced property.
It is useful for situations where the Grid requires additional, overlayed UI (such as a Gantt chart or a calendar application).
The easiest way to override it is to decorate defaultCellRangeRenderer.
 Defaults to defaultCellRangeRenderer.

headings.title: children
headings.text:
One or more Columns describing the data displayed in this table.
Falsy children are ignored, to allow easier dynamic showing/hiding of columns.
 Table reads the props of its children (with defaultColumnProps applied) without rendering them,
so components that wrap Column (e.g. const MyColumn = (props: ColumnProps) => <Column {...props} />) can be used as children too.
(Subclassing Column is no longer supported.)

headings.title: className
headings.text: Optional custom CSS class name to attach to root Table element.

headings.title: containerProps
headings.text: Additional props (eg onWheel) to spread onto the outer Grid element.

headings.title: containerRole
headings.text: ARIA role for the inner cell-container.

headings.title: containerStyle
headings.text: Optional custom inline style to attach to inner cell-container element.

headings.title: deferredMeasurementCache
headings.text:
If CellMeasurer is used to measure this Table's cells, this should be a pointer to its CellMeasurerCache.
It is passed through to the inner Grid.

headings.title: disableHeader
headings.text: Do not render the table header (only the rows).

headings.title: estimatedRowSize
headings.text:
Used to estimate the total height of a Table before all of its rows have actually been measured.
The estimated total height is adjusted as rows are rendered.

headings.title: getScrollbarSize
headings.text:
Returns the size of the browser's scrollbar.
Exposed for testing purposes only.
 Defaults to measuring (and caching) the width of the browser's native scrollbar.

headings.title: gridClassName
headings.text: Optional custom CSS class name to attach to inner Grid element.

headings.title: gridStyle
headings.text: Optional inline style to attach to inner Grid element.

headings.title: headerClassName
headings.text: Optional CSS class to apply to all column headers.

headings.title: headerHeight
headings.text: Fixed height of header row.

headings.title: headerRowRenderer
headings.text:
Responsible for rendering the table header row given an array of columns:
({ className: string, columns: ReactNode[], style: CSSProperties }): ReactNode.
 This is an advanced property.
It is useful for situations where you require additional hooks into Table to render additional custom UI elements.
You may want to start by forking the defaultTableHeaderRowRenderer function (the default).

headings.title: headerStyle
headings.text: Optional custom inline style to attach to table header columns.

headings.title: height
headings.text:
Fixed/available height for the outer DOM element.
Required, unless a scrollElement is specified.
 With a scrollElement, the height of the scroll element's viewport is used instead;
this prop is then only used until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering).

headings.title: id
headings.text: Optional custom id to attach to root Table element.

headings.title: initialScrollTop
headings.text:
Vertical scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Table at.
Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll).
This also works with server rendering: the rows at this offset are rendered on the server,
and they stay in place when the page is hydrated.
Ignored if a scrollElement is specified (which then determines the vertical offset).

headings.title: isScrollingOptOut
headings.text:
Prevents re-rendering of visible cells on scroll end.
(Opts out of the isScrolling param passed to cellRangeRenderer, to avoid the extra render when scroll stops.)
Visible cells are still re-rendered when the Grid's props change or forceUpdate() is called.

headings.title: noRowsRenderer
headings.text: Optional renderer to be used in place of table body rows when rowCount is 0.

headings.title: onColumnClick
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user clicks on a table column (cell):
({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, event: Event }): void.

headings.title: onHeaderClick
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user clicks on (or activates via the ENTER or SPACE key) a table header:
({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, event: Event }): void.

headings.title: onRowClick
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user clicks on a table row:
({ event: Event, index: number, rowData: any }): void.

headings.title: onRowDoubleClick
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user double-clicks on a table row:
({ event: Event, index: number, rowData: any }): void.

headings.title: onRowMouseOut
headings.text:
Callback invoked when the mouse leaves a table row:
({ event: Event, index: number, rowData: any }): void.

headings.title: onRowMouseOver
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user moves the mouse over a table row:
({ event: Event, index: number, rowData: any }): void.

headings.title: onRowRightClick
headings.text:
Callback invoked when a user right-clicks on a table row:
({ event: Event, index: number, rowData: any }): void.

headings.title: onRowsRendered
headings.text:
Callback invoked with information about the slice of rows that were just rendered:
({ overscanStartIndex: number, overscanStopIndex: number, startIndex: number, stopIndex: number }): void.

headings.title: onScroll
headings.text:
Callback invoked whenever the scroll offset changes within the inner scrollable region:
({ clientHeight: number, scrollHeight: number, scrollTop: number }): void.
This callback can be used to sync scrolling between lists, tables, or grids.

headings.title: onScrollbarPresenceChange
headings.text:
Called whenever a horizontal or vertical scrollbar is added or removed:
({ horizontal: boolean, size: number, vertical: boolean }): void.
This prop is not intended for end-user use;
it is used by MultiGrid to support fixed-row/fixed-column scroll syncing.

headings.title: overscanIndicesGetter
headings.text:
Responsible for calculating the number of rows to overscan before and after a specified range (see Grid overscanIndicesGetter).
By default (accessibilityOverscanIndicesGetter), Table overscans by at least one row in each direction (for accessibility).

headings.title: overscanRowCount
headings.text:
Number of rows to render above/below the visible bounds of the list.
This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

headings.title: rowClassName
headings.text:
Optional CSS class to apply to all table rows (including the header row).
This value may be either a static string or a function with the signature ({ index: number }): string.
Note that for the header row an index of -1 is provided.

headings.title: rowRenderer
headings.text:
Responsible for rendering a table row given an array of columns.
 This is an advanced property.
It is useful for situations where you require additional hooks into Table (eg integration with a library like react-sortable-hoc).
The easiest way to override it is to decorate (or fork) the defaultTableRowRenderer function (the default).

headings.title: rowStyle
headings.text:
Optional custom inline style to attach to table rows (including the header row).
This value may be either a style object or a function with the signature ({ index: number }): CSSProperties.
Note that for the header row an index of -1 is provided.

headings.title: scrollElement
headings.text:
Element that scrolls the Table (instead of the Table scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element
(e.g. a container that the Table is rendered within, along with other content).
 The Table then renders all of its rows at their full height (below its header, which scrolls along with them), renders only the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport,
and its scroll methods scroll the scroll element.
Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the Table re-renders
(e.g. call forceUpdateGrid() if content above the Table changes size without the Table re-rendering).
Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached);
the Table then renders the rows at its top.

headings.title: scrollingResetTimeInterval
headings.text: Wait this amount of time (in milliseconds) after the last scroll event before resetting Grid pointer-events.

headings.title: sort
headings.text:
Sort function to be called if a sortable header is clicked:
({ defaultSortDirection: SortDirection, event: Event, sortBy: string, sortDirection: SortDirection }): void.

headings.title: sortBy
headings.text: Data is currently sorted by this dataKey (if it is sorted at all).

headings.title: sortDirection
headings.text: Data is currently sorted in this direction (if it is sorted at all).

headings.title: style
headings.text: Optional custom inline style to attach to root Table element.

headings.title: tabIndex
headings.text: Optional override of inner Grid tab index default.

text:
Table component with fixed headers and virtualized rows for improved performance with large data sets.
This component expects explicit width, height, and padding parameters.
 Columns are described by Column children (or components that render a Column).
Scrolling is done through the imperative handle (ref): see scrollToRow, scrollToCell, and scrollToPosition.
title: Table component props

text: For more control than rowClassName and rowStyle offer, Table accepts a rowRenderer and a headerRowRenderer. These are advanced properties, useful when you need additional hooks into Table (e.g. integrating with a drag-and-drop library like react-sortable-hoc) or need to render additional UI elements. The easiest way to override them is to decorate the default implementations, defaultTableRowRenderer and defaultTableHeaderRowRenderer, or to fork them. Click a row below to select it: A headerRowRenderer is passed the header row className, style, and the rendered columns. A rowRenderer is passed the same values plus the row index, key, rowData, isScrolling, and the onRowClick, onRowDoubleClick, onRowMouseOut, onRowMouseOver, and onRowRightClick handlers. A custom row renderer must apply the style it is passed to the row element; it positions the row within the table.
title: Custom rows

headings.title: Class names
headings.text: Class names Table renders the following static class names, which can be targeted by your styles: ReactVirtualized__Table: main (outer) element ReactVirtualized__Table__Grid: inner Grid (the scrollable body) ReactVirtualized__Table__headerRow: header row (similar to thead > tr) ReactVirtualized__Table__headerColumn: header cell (similar to thead > tr > th) ReactVirtualized__Table__sortableHeaderColumn: applied to header cells that are sortable ReactVirtualized__Table__headerTruncatedText: header label rendered by the default header renderer ReactVirtualized__Table__sortableHeaderIcon: SVG sort indicator (plus --ASC or --DESC modifier) ReactVirtualized__Table__row: table row (similar to tbody > tr) ReactVirtualized__Table__rowColumn: table cell (similar to tbody > tr > td)

text: Rows can be styled using the rowClassName and rowStyle props, and their heights can be fixed or vary from row to row. The table below has sortable headers, a custom header and cell renderer, alternating row styles, optional dynamic row heights, and a placeholder that is shown when there are no rows. Dynamic row heights Hide index column Hide header No rows rowClassName (and rowStyle) can be a static value or a function of the row index. They are also applied to the header row, which is passed an index of -1. rowHeight can be a fixed number or a function of the row index. If row heights change after they have been measured, call recomputeRowHeights . Falsy children are ignored, so columns can be shown or hidden conditionally. noRowsRenderer renders placeholder content when rowCount is 0. The headerClassName prop applies a class to every column header (normal-case above overrides the default uppercase style). Sorting is covered in more detail on the sorting page.
title: Row styles and heights

headings.title: SortDirection
headings.text: SortDirection The SortDirection constant specifies which direction data is sorted in: SortDirection.ASC ("ASC") sorts items in ascending order, from the lowest value to the highest (e.g. a-z, 0-9). SortDirection.DESC ("DESC") sorts items in descending order, from the highest value to the lowest (e.g. z-a, 9-0).

headings.title: SortIndicator
headings.text: SortIndicator The default header renderer shows a SortIndicator (an arrow icon) beside the label of the column the table is sorted by. If you render custom headers, you can use SortIndicator to show the sort direction yourself:

headings.title: Returning to the natural order
headings.text: Returning to the natural order Once a Table has been sorted, the built-in sort directions only toggle between ascending and descending; there is no way to return to the unsorted, “natural” order. The natural sort tables guide shows how to implement this in your application code.

headings.title: Sorting by multiple columns
headings.text: Sorting by multiple columns By default, Table assumes that its data will be sorted by a single attribute. The createTableMultiSort utility can be used to sort by multiple fields; see the multi-column sort tables guide. Sorting large data sets can be expensive; memoize the sorted data (e.g. with useMemo) so that it is only re-sorted when the sort criteria change.

text: Table headers can be made sortable. Click a column header below to sort by it; click it again to reverse the sort direction. Table does not sort data itself. Instead, it tells you how the data should be sorted, and renders the current sort state: sort is called when a sortable header is clicked (or activated with the ENTER or SPACE key). It is passed the sortBy (the clicked column's dataKey) and the suggested sortDirection, as well as the column's defaultSortDirection and the DOM event. Sort your data accordingly, and update your state to re-render the table. sortBy is the dataKey that data is currently sorted by (if it is sorted at all). sortDirection is the direction data is currently sorted in (if it is sorted at all). Headers are only sortable if a sort function is provided. Individual columns can opt out with the disableSort prop. A column's defaultSortDirection ("ASC" by default) controls the suggested direction when it is first clicked; clicking it again suggests the opposite direction. See Column props for more.
title: Sorting

headings.title: Grid, Table and Masonry
headings.text: Grid, Table and Masonry The scrollElement prop works the same way for a Grid. The window only scrolls a Grid vertically; if its columns are wider than its width, it still scrolls horizontally itself: A Table's header row is scrolled along with its rows (it doesn't stay at the top of the window): For a Masonry, reset the cell positioner when the available width changes (e.g. in AutoSizer's onResize), so that the number of columns fits the new width: MultiGrid always scrolls itself, so it doesn't have a scrollElement prop.

headings.title: Scrolling to a row
headings.text: Scrolling to a row A component with a scrollElement is scrolled with its regular methods: the List or Table's scrollToRow and scrollToPosition, or the Grid's scrollToCell and scrollToPosition. They scroll the scroll element (e.g. the window) instead of the component itself, so a regular ref is all that's needed. (This page is itself part of a larger layout, so the example below scrolls a container; see scrolling an element.) Things to keep in mind: These are one-time scrolls: the row isn't kept in view if row heights change afterwards. Offsets passed to scrollToPosition (and returned by getOffsetForRow) are relative to the top of the list, not to the top of the page. To scroll to a row that is being added, call scrollToRow once the list has rendered it (e.g. in an effect). Rows that haven't been measured yet (e.g. by CellMeasurer) are positioned using their estimated heights, so the row may not end up exactly aligned. The list's position within the scroll element is measured again each time it scrolls it, so content above the list that has changed size is taken into account. A Grid is only scrolled vertically by its scroll element; if it is wider than its width, it still scrolls horizontally itself. scrollToRow scrolls immediately. headings.title: Height
headings.text: Height The height prop is optional with a scroll element: the height of the scroll element's viewport (e.g. the window's) is used to determine which rows to render. If a height is passed, it is only used until the scroll element has been measured, e.g. during server rendering, or while scrollElement is null because the element isn't available yet. (The component then renders its top rows, at its full height.)

headings.title: Content above the component
headings.text: Content above the component The component's position within the scroll element (e.g. how far it is from the top of the page) is measured again whenever the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and whenever the component re-renders. If content above it changes size without the component re-rendering (e.g. a banner is dismissed, and the component's props don't change), re-render it with forceUpdateGrid() (List and Table) or forceUpdate() (Grid and Masonry): Until the component re-renders (or the scroll element scrolls), it renders the rows for its previous position, so part of the viewport may be left empty. How likely this is depends on the browser: while the page is scrolled, browsers that support scroll anchoring (e.g. Chrome and Firefox) adjust the scroll position when content above changes size, which re-measures the component; browsers without scroll anchoring (e.g. Safari) don't. The rows rendered beyond the viewport (see the overscanRowCount prop) hide small changes, but not content above the component growing. So call forceUpdateGrid() or forceUpdate() whenever content above the component may change size.

headings.title: Migrating from WindowScroller
headings.text: Migrating from WindowScroller In version 10, the WindowScroller component has been replaced by the scrollElement prop. Instead of wrapping the component in a WindowScroller and wiring its render parameters to the autoHeight, height, isScrolling, onScroll and scrollTop props (all of which have been removed, except height and onScroll), pass scrollElement directly: What replaced each part of the WindowScroller API: registerChild (and the wrapper element it was attached to): not needed; the component measures its position from its own element. Use a regular ref to call its methods. height (and width): the viewport height is measured by the component itself. Use AutoSizer for the width (the window's width usually isn't the width available to the component). scrollTop, isScrolling and onChildScroll: handled by the component. isScrolling is still passed to the rowRenderer (or cellRenderer). scrollLeft: horizontal window scrolling is no longer supported. The scrollElement prop: moved to the component, and accepts "window" (instead of the window object) or an element. updatePosition(): not needed; the position is measured again on every scroll, on resize, and whenever the component re-renders (see "Content above the component" above). updateScrollTopOnUpdatePosition is no longer needed either. onScroll: use the component's own onScroll prop, which reports how far the scroll element has been scrolled past the top of the component. onResize: use a resize event listener on the window (or a ResizeObserver on the scroll element). serverHeight and serverWidth: pass height (used until the scroll element has been measured) and width to the component. scrollingResetTimeInterval: use the scrollingResetTimeInterval prop of the Grid, List or Masonry. IS_SCROLLING_TIMEOUT and defaultWindowScrollerProps: removed.

text: A List, Grid, Table or Masonry can be scrolled by the window (rather than having a scrollbar of its own) by setting its scrollElement prop to "window". This can be used to create layouts similar to Facebook or Twitter news feeds, where the list scrolls along with the rest of the page. With a scroll element, the component: renders at its full height (it doesn't scroll itself vertically), renders only the rows (or cells) visible within the window's viewport, and its scroll methods (scrollToRow, scrollToCell and scrollToPosition) scroll the window; see scrolling to a row. A regular ref can be used to call its methods. Only the width needs to be provided, e.g. by AutoSizer: The window is the most common scroll element, but any scrollable element can be used instead; see scrolling an element (which also has a live example).
title: Scrolling with the page

text: Instead of "window", the scrollElement prop can be a scrollable element (e.g. a container with overflow: auto that the component is rendered within, along with other content). The component then scrolls along with the rest of that element's content, and renders only the rows visible within the element. The component needs the element itself (not a ref object), so store it in state with a ref callback; this re-renders the component once the element has been mounted. Until then, the scrollElement is null, and the component renders its top rows (at its full height). In the example below, the content above the list and the list itself share a single scrollbar (the container's); the list doesn't have a scrollbar of its own. Size changes of the scroll element are detected with a ResizeObserver, and the component's position within it is measured again whenever it scrolls.
